_readme: Gauge provenance: the human audit trail behind aliases.json.
Each entry under `gauges` is keyed `source:site` (lookupGauge's gaugeKey) and
records that the owner personally verified this station is the correct,
commonly used gauge for the run(s) that reference it. The machine can prove a
gauge is alive and fresh (src/canarySweep.ts); only a paddler can prove it is
the RIGHT gauge. test/provenance.test.ts enforces coverage via an inverted
ratchet: lower MAX_UNAUDITED there as entries are added; 0 = fully enforcing.
`rituals` records the seasonal real-device tests: a real InReach round trip
pre-season and mid-season, the only check that exercises the Garmin POST.

usgs:12359800.notes: SF Flathead ab Twin Creek — the free-flowing wilderness reach (Youngs Creek/Bob Marshall multiday + Meadow Creek Gorge). AW quotes this gauge for both sections. NOT 12362500 (Columbia Falls), which is Hungry Horse dam outflow on a different reach. Live-verified 5,340 cfs / 8.63 ft at add time.

envdata:Wairaurahiri at Lake Hauroko.notes: Owen supplied the exact envdata.es.govt.nz share link for this run. Live-verified 45.0 m3/sec at add time via the site's own services/data.ashx JSON endpoint (reverse-engineered from base.js — no public API docs). Site is identified by exact name string, no numeric code.

flowrate:61.notes: Owen corrected this: the physical gauge sits on the Haast mainstem (flowrate.co.nz labels it 'Haast River — Roaring Billy'), a few km below the Haast/Landsborough confluence, but the run paddlers actually use it for is the Landsborough R — per packraftingtrips.nz/landsborough, published bands at Roaring Billy are 50-85 cumecs very low, 85-100 low/good, 100-150 moderate (our low/high), 150-250 high/experts only. Live-verified 93.5 m3/sec at add time via flowrate.co.nz/station/61/json/flow/current; page confirms units as Cumecs (m3/s).

usgs:09402500.notes: Colorado R near Grand Canyon (Phantom Ranch) — mid-canyon reference for the Grand Canyon trip. Note the USGS station name is literally 'COLORADO RIVER NEAR GRAND CANYON, AZ', named for the South Rim village: as a LOCATION 'grand canyon' means this station, while as a run name it means Lees Ferry. Hence the qualified aliases (grand canyon at grand canyon, colorado at grand canyon) resolving here.

wsc:08CE001.notes: Stikine Grand Canyon at Telegraph Creek. Range audit 2026-07-09: previous 400-1500 cms band showed GOOD at 920 cms, badly wrong for a class V+ expedition river. Corrected to 225-550 per Owen + the Oracle model itself (weth watch.py Q=550, the window-opens threshold; forecast card says 'good under 550 cms') + bcwhitewater.org reach 58 ('generally paddled 250-450 cms, 350 optimal'). Live-verified 920 cms reading HIGH after fix.

wsc:08EF005.notes: Clore Grand Canyon, quoted off the Zymoetz above O.K. Creek gauge (the Clore itself is ungauged; it is the Zymoetz's major tributary). Range audit 2026-07-09: previous 50-200 guess showed GOOD at 190 cms. Corrected to 100-150 per bcwhitewater.org/reaches/clore-river-grand-canyon: 'The Zymoetz River should be between 100-150 cms for the Clore to be runnable.' Late-summer fly-in classic; high water = continuous class V.

wsc:08CG001.notes: Iskut below Johnson River. Range audit 2026-07-09: NO runnable band on this station on purpose. Paddler beta (bcwhitewater.org/reaches/74-iskut-river) judges the run off the STIKINE gauge ('paddle when the Stikine is a bit high, 400-600 cms') plus a roadside gauge rock near Burrage Creek - nobody quotes the Johnson station, which sits below major tributaries and runs ~1000+ cms in season. Previous 100-500 band was fabricated and read HIGH year-round. Grey/no-range is the honest display; the gauge stays for trend/reference.

usgs:15292000.notes: Susitna at Gold Creek (Devils Canyon). Range audit 2026-07-09: NO runnable band on purpose. Previous 3000-10000 cfs guess called the documented ideal flow HIGH - americanwhitewater.org/content/River/detail/id/46 cites ideal kayak flows ~15,000 cfs, but no published min/max band exists for this once-a-generation class V+ run, and the river can rise 15,000 cfs in hours. Grey/no-range until someone with firsthand Devils Canyon knowledge sets a receipted band.

usgs:13246000.notes: North Fork Payette nr Banks — the Banks gauge is the standard reference for the Smiths Ferry-to-Banks class V run. Station specified by the owner when the run was added. Runnable band 400-3000 cfs from American Whitewater reach 592 (Payette, N. Fork / 5. Smiths Ferry to Banks), which correlates to this same USGS station.

usgs:13235000.notes: South Fork Payette at Lowman — station specified by the owner when the run was added. Runnable band 600-5000 cfs from American Whitewater reach 593 (Payette, S. Fork / 1. Grandjean to Deadwood), the reach AW correlates to this station. Caveat: AW keys the downstream Canyon/Staircase reaches to a CALCULATED gauge below the Deadwood confluence, not to Lowman, so this band describes the reach above Deadwood.

usgs:09404200.notes: Colorado R above Diamond Creek nr Peach Springs — the Grand Canyon takeout gauge (river mile 226), completing the trip's three reference points alongside Lees Ferry (put-in, 09380000) and Phantom Ranch (mid-canyon, 09402500). Station specified by the owner. Runnable band mirrors the other two GC rows: one dam release, one trip.

usgs:09371010.notes: San Juan R at Four Corners — upstream indicator for the San Juan trip, not its own run: water here reaches Bluff/Sand Island roughly a day later, so it is the early read for a launch decision. Station specified by the owner. Band mirrors the Bluff row (500-5000) because it is the same river and trip and the two gauges track closely (662 vs 560 cfs when added); American Whitewater publishes no reach correlated to this station that could be cited instead.
